q: What is the name of Figure A, which is located in Ilocos Norte?
n: Figure A is Paoay Church (San Agustin, 1694–1710) in Ilocos Norte, an Earthquake Baroque church with massive buttresses. Source: UNESCO (Baroque Churches of the Philippines).

q: What is the name of Figure B, which is located in Albay?
n: Figure B is Daraga Church (Nuestra Señora de la Porteria) in Albay, a Baroque church built of volcanic stone facing Mayon Volcano. Source: National Museum of the Philippines (National Cultural Treasure).

q: What is the name of Figure C, which is located in Cebu?
o: Our Lady of Mount Carmel Church
n: Figure C is the Basilica Minore del Santo Niño in Cebu City, founded in 1565 and home of the Santo Niño de Cebu. Source: Basilica del Santo Niño official site; NHCP.

q: What is the name of Figure D, which is located in Intramuros, Manila?
n: Figure D is San Agustin Church in Intramuros (1587–1607), the oldest stone church in the Philippines. Source: UNESCO (Baroque Churches of the Philippines).

q: What is the name of Figure E, which is located in Quiapo, Manila?
n: Figure E is the San Sebastian Basilica in Quiapo, Manila (1891), the only all-steel Gothic Revival church in Asia. Source: NHCP; National Museum (National Cultural Treasure).

q: How many Filipino National Artists for Architecture were there as of December 2019?
n: As of December 2019 there were six National Artists for Architecture: Juan Nakpil (1973), Pablo Antonio (1976), Leandro Locsin (1990), Ildefonso Santos Jr. (landscape, 2006), José María Zaragoza (2014) and Francisco Mañosa (2018). Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists.

q: Who was the first National Artist for Architecture?
n: Juan F. Nakpil was the first National Artist for Architecture, proclaimed in 1973. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists.

q: Who was the most recent National Artist for Architecture as of December 2019?
n: Francisco T. Mañosa, proclaimed in 2018, was the most recent National Artist for Architecture as of December 2019. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists.

q: Which architect was known for championing indigenous Filipino materials?
n: Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa championed indigenous Filipino materials and forms (bamboo, coconut, capiz, nipa), as in the Coconut Palace. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists; Mañosa & Co.

q: Who designed the Manila Jockey Club, Rufino Building, and the University of the Philippines Administration and Library?
n: Juan F. Nakpil designed the Manila Jockey Club, the Rufino Building and the UP Administration (Quezon Hall) and Main Library buildings in Diliman. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Juan F. Nakpil).

q: Who designed the Philam Life Building?
n: Carlos Arguelles designed the Philam Life Building on United Nations Avenue, Manila (1961). Source: Philippine architecture histories (Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino).

q: Who designed the GSIS Building in Pasay?
n: Jorge Ramos designed the GSIS Headquarters Building in Pasay (1996). Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Who designed the Philippine Heart Center?
n: Jorge Ramos designed the Philippine Heart Center in Quezon City (1975). Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Who designed Santo Domingo Church in Quezon City?
n: José María Zaragoza designed Santo Domingo Church in Quezon City (1954), a modern Spanish Mission and Gothic church. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Zaragoza).

q: Who designed many of the Iglesia ni Cristo's signature churches?
n: Carlos Santos-Viola designed many Iglesia ni Cristo chapels, including the Central Temple. Their tall spires and fins are the church's signature. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Which Filipino architect is famous for Brutalism?
n: Leandro Locsin is the Filipino architect best known for Brutalist concrete, as at the CCP Theater of Performing Arts and the Folk Arts Theater. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Locsin).

q: Which Filipino architect is known for floating volumes?
n: Locsin's work is known for "floating volumes," heavy concrete masses that seem to hover on recessed bases, as at the CCP. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Locsin); Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Who is the first dean of Filipino architects?
n: Juan Nakpil is called the dean of Filipino architects. He was the first National Artist for Architecture (1973). Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Juan F. Nakpil).

q: Who was proclaimed National Artist for Architecture in 2018?
n: Francisco Mañosa was proclaimed National Artist for Architecture in 2018. Zaragoza was proclaimed in 2014. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists.

q: Which Filipino architect is known for neo-vernacular design?
n: Francisco Mañosa developed a neo-vernacular Filipino architecture, reinterpreting the bahay kubo and indigenous materials in modern buildings. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Mañosa).

q: Who was the PRC's 2022 Outstanding Professional of the Year in Architecture?
n: The PRC named Ar. Gerard Rey A. Lico its 2022 Outstanding Professional of the Year in Architecture. Source: Professional Regulation Commission, 2022 Outstanding Professionals awards.

q: Who received the UAP Likha Award and Gold Medal in 2022?
n: Ar. Jose Siao Ling received the UAP Likha Award (Gold Medal), the UAP's highest award, in 2022. Source: United Architects of the Philippines, 2022 national convention awards.

q: Which of these is a National Artist for Architecture?
n: Francisco Mañosa is a National Artist for Architecture (2018). Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists.

q: Which architect received the PRC Eric Nubla Excellence Award in 2021?
n: Ar. Jose Pedro C. Recio received the PRC's Eric Nubla Excellence Award in 2021, given through the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture. Source: Professional Regulation Commission awards announcements (2021).

q: Who was the first registered Filipino architect?
n: Tomás Mapúa was the first registered architect in the Philippines, licensed under Act No. 2985 of 1921. He founded Mapúa Institute of Technology. Source: NHCP; Mapúa University history.

q: Which Filipino architect studied abroad and began practice in 1858?
n: Félix Roxas y Arroyo studied in Spain and began practice in Manila around 1858. He is regarded as the first Filipino architect. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino; NHCP.

q: Who was named the first National Artist for Architecture in 1973?
n: Juan F. Nakpil was named the first National Artist for Architecture in 1973. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists.

q: Who was the first Likha Awardee in 1982?
n: Felipe M. Mendoza, architect of the Batasang Pambansa Complex, was the first recipient of the UAP Likha Award in 1982. Source: United Architects of the Philippines (Likha Award roll).

q: Who designed the Art Deco Crystal Arcade on Escolta?
n: Andrés Luna de San Pedro, son of painter Juan Luna, designed the Art Deco Crystal Arcade on Escolta (1932). Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino; Escolta heritage records.

q: Who is the first registered female Filipino architect in the Philippines?
n: Mercedes Raffiñan, licensed in 1934 (License No. 45), was the first registered female architect in the Philippines. Source: PRC/UAP historical records; Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Which key government building in Manila did Antonio Toledo design?
n: Antonio Toledo designed Manila City Hall, completed in 1941 during the American period, with its distinctive clock tower. Source: NHCP; Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Which is the oldest stone church still standing in the Philippines?
n: San Agustín Church in Intramuros (1586–1607) is the oldest stone church still standing in the Philippines. Source: UNESCO (Baroque Churches of the Philippines).

q: Who is often called the Dean of Filipino Architects and was the first National Artist for Architecture?
n: Juan F. Nakpil is often called the Dean of Filipino Architects. He was the first National Artist for Architecture (1973). Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists.

q: Who designed UP's Church of the Risen Lord, praised in the 1950s for its double parabola?
n: Cesar Concio designed UP Diliman's Church of the Risen Lord (1955), noted for its double-parabolic concrete shell form. Source: UP Diliman heritage records; Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Who designed the Quezon Memorial Shrine?
n: Federico Ilustre designed the Quezon Memorial Shrine in Quezon City, whose 66 m pylon is one metre for each year of President Quezon's life. Source: NHCP (Quezon Memorial Shrine).

q: Who is the architect of the Pearl Farm Beach Resort in Samal?
n: Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa designed the Pearl Farm Beach Resort on Samal Island, Davao, with indigenous-inspired forms and materials. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists (Mañosa); Mañosa & Co.

q: The first neo-vernacular government building in the Philippines.
n: Cotabato City Hall, with Maranao-inspired domes and ornament, is cited as the first neo-vernacular government building in the Philippines. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: The architect of the WHO Headquarters in Manila.
n: Alfredo J. Luz designed the WHO Western Pacific Regional Office headquarters on United Nations Avenue, Manila (1959). Source: WHO WPRO history; Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino.

q: Which building is considered the first earthquake-resistant building in the Philippines?
n: The UST Main Building (1927), designed by Fr. Roque Ruaño, OP, was built as separate sections joined by expansion joints and is considered the first earthquake-resistant building in the Philippines. Source: University of Santo Tomas; National Museum (National Cultural Treasure).

q: What is considered Leandro Locsin's first major work?
n: Leandro Locsin's first major work was the Church of the Holy Sacrifice at UP Diliman (1955), a round chapel with a thin-shell concrete dome. Source: National Museum (National Historical Landmark); NCCA (Locsin).
